tasks.short: As mentor, spot students with problems or special interests, talk with them, agree steps and inform parents.

steps.what: Mentor notices students with problems from grades, absence and colleagues' remarks
Mentor reads the student's grades, absence and notes in the student records
Mentor holds a one-to-one conversation to guide and counsel the student
Mentor consults the care coordinator or year head on support or subject choice
Care coordinator advises on support, referral or subject options
Mentor logs the agreements in the student file
Mentor e-mails or phones parents about the agreements
Mentor follows up the agreements in a later conversation

tasks.design: Fixed rules on the student information system ({OTHER}) build a weekly signal list per mentor group (grade drop, absence, lateness, flagged colleague notes) and a one-page student overview. Agreements go into a short form with owner and follow-up date that reminds the mentor and fills a parent message template for the mentor to edit and send.
tasks.previous_blocker: Signals were spread over grade lists, absence screens and e-mails, so mentors noticed problems late.
tasks.enabler_now: Student information systems export grades and absence, and fixed rules and templates are quick to build.
tasks.still_hard: Trust and the conversation are the work; rules flag symptoms and miss quiet students.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what a teenager does not say and knowing when to involve parents or the care team.

ambition.what: Students with a special academic interest flagged by grades too, so they get an enrichment talk, not only those who struggle.

tasks.altitude: The mentor spends less time hunting for signals and writing; decisions on support stay with mentor and care coordinator.

reach.learn: Whether the same signal rules suit younger students.

evidence.claim: Pupil data sits in Dutch school information systems, and a report is a query plus a template.
Under the school participation act, parents and students consent to rules on pupil data.
Support needs are health data, and new pupil-data processing needs a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: from noticing a signal to agreements followed up; formal care referrals are outside.

Input contract: grades entered by subject teachers, absence registered per lesson, colleague notes in the student information system; signal thresholds set by the care coordinator; fallback is the mentor's own checks.
Rules are fixed thresholds, not AI scoring of students.
Care coordinator and parent time is outside the mentor's savings.
unknowns: Whether the school's student information system allows custom signal queries.
How many mentor students each teacher has.
research_questions: Do signal lists bring mentor conversations earlier in the term?

already_counted.description: Mentor reviews the weekly signal list and dismisses false signals.
Mentor checks the generated overview before the conversation.

incremental.description: Mentor keeps agreements and follow-up dates current.
Care coordinator tunes signal thresholds each term.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Mentors with small groups already know their students, so the signal list saves little; conversations take most time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Use slides, video, simulations and classroom equipment to support lessons, and fix technical problems.

steps.what: Teacher finds or makes slides, videos and simulations to supplement presentations

loop.input: The lesson objectives and the textbook section text chosen by the teacher.
loop.output: Draft slide text with one point per slide and suggested image or video searches.
loop.check: Each slide maps to a lesson objective; key terms and numbers on a slide must appear in the textbook section; the teacher reviews every slide.
loop.stop: One redraft; then the teacher builds the slides.
loop.why_not_simpler: Summarising a textbook section into slides is writing; a template only gives the layout.

steps.what: Teacher sets up computers, projector or board and sound before class
Teacher presents with slides, clips and demonstrations
Teacher troubleshoots equipment problems or calls the ICT helpdesk
ICT support repairs the classroom equipment

tasks.design: A shared slide library per course in {DOCS}, tagged by lesson goal, plus a bounded model step that drafts slides from the lesson objectives and the textbook section for the teacher to review. Classroom PCs get a one-click lesson profile that starts the board, sound and the lesson file, and a QR code in each room opens a pre-filled fault form in the {HELPDESK}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each teacher built slides alone, and classroom setups differed per room.
tasks.enabler_now: Lesson editors summarise and rewrite text, a trial with secondary science teachers showed shorter planning time, and device management can push a standard room profile.
tasks.still_hard: Good presentations depend on the teacher's story and timing; drafts can be bland or slightly wrong.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the image or demo that makes a concept click and reading when to stop the slides.

ambition.what: Department colleagues reuse and improve each other's slides every term instead of each starting from scratch.

tasks.altitude: The teacher reviews and adapts slides rather than building them alone; presenting does not change.

reach.learn: Which rooms produce most fault reports and why.

evidence.claim: A Dutch lesson editor rewrites text at another level, summarises and translates.
A randomised trial with 259 secondary science teachers cut weekly planning from 81.5 to 56.2 minutes with a chatbot and guide, with no quality difference.
A school that adapts an AI tool can become its provider under the AI Act.
Using images and clips in lessons relies on the education exception in copyright law, with national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from preparing presentation materials to the lesson presented and faults reported; repairs are outside.
Input contract: lesson objectives from the course outline; textbook sections the school licenses; slides uploaded by department colleagues with goal tags; fallback is building slides alone.
No pupil data goes into the draft step.
ICT support time is outside the teacher's savings.
unknowns: Whether the school's licence allows textbook text in a model service.
research_questions: Do shared slide libraries keep being used after the first term?

already_counted.description: Teacher reviews drafted slides for accuracy and fit.

incremental.description: Teacher tags and uploads slides to the shared library.
ICT keeps room profiles and the fault form working.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Teachers with mature slide sets save little on drafting, and rooms with old equipment keep setup problems.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write course objectives, the week-by-week outline and the testing programme, following the exam syllabus and school rules.

steps.what: Teacher reads the exam syllabus and school curriculum requirements for the course
Teacher agrees the year planning with department colleagues
Teacher writes course objectives and the week-by-week outlines

loop.input: The syllabus objective codes assigned to this year, the textbook chapter list and the school calendar.
loop.output: Course objectives in student language and a week-by-week outline with chapters, activities and homework.
loop.check: Each objective maps to a syllabus code; every code assigned to the year appears at least once; week numbers, holidays and test weeks match the calendar; the teacher reviews all text.
loop.stop: Two redrafts; then the teacher writes the outline.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning syllabus codes into objectives students understand and a sensible weekly flow is writing; a template only gives the grid.

steps.what: Teacher writes the testing programme entries: tests, weights and dates
Department head checks outline and testing programme against exam rules and approves
Teacher publishes the course outline in the learning environment
Teacher updates the outline when dates change during the year

tasks.design: The exam syllabus is held as a coded objective list per year in {DOCS}; a bounded model step drafts course objectives and a weekly outline from the assigned codes, the textbook chapters and the school calendar, and a deterministic generator builds testing-programme entries whose weights and dates are checked against the rules. After the department head approves, the outline publishes to the {LMS} and regenerates when calendar dates change.
tasks.previous_blocker: Outlines were rewritten each year by hand from syllabus documents and last year's files.
tasks.enabler_now: Syllabus objectives can be held as a coded list, and language models draft objectives and outlines that a code check can verify.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the order and depth of topics is professional judgement; syllabus changes must be entered by someone.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding what matters most for these students and pacing the year realistically.

ambition.what: Outlines adjusted each term from test results and calendar changes, not fixed for the year.

tasks.altitude: The teacher reviews and adjusts outlines rather than writing them; the department head approves from checked material.

reach.task: Check the school's testing programme against exam rules
reach.learn: Whether the deterministic weight and date checks catch what coordinators now check by hand.

evidence.claim: Core goals can be held as a fixed list, a model drafts objectives, and a check maps each objective to a goal code.
A randomised trial with 259 secondary science teachers cut weekly planning from 81.5 to 56.2 minutes, with no quality difference.
A randomised trial with 464 primary teachers cut preparation 24%, but the tool covered 7% of lessons and use declined.
The testing programme for exam classes must be set and published by a national deadline under exam rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from reading the syllabus to the outline published and kept current; teaching is outside.

Input contract: syllabus objective codes per year, entered by the department head from the national syllabus; textbook chapter list; school calendar from the timetabler; fallback is last year's outline.
Department head time is outside the teacher's savings.
unknowns: Whether syllabus codes are already listed per year in the department.
How much of the outline the school prescribes.
research_questions: After a year, do teachers keep using drafted outlines or revert to last year's files?

already_counted.description: Teacher reviews drafted objectives and outline.
Teacher checks generated testing programme entries.

incremental.description: Teacher corrects code mappings and reports poor drafts.
Department head keeps syllabus codes and the rules list current.

approvals.approved_version: Course outline and testing programme entries as approved by the department head in s5; later edits need a new approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: As in the primary trial, teachers may use drafts for part of their courses only, and stable courses already reuse last year's outline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set homework and class work, mark it, give feedback and enter the grades.

steps.what: Teacher assigns homework and class work in the learning environment
Students hand in work on paper or in the learning environment
Teacher marks closed questions against the answer key
Teacher grades open answers and essays against the rubric

loop.input: One student's answer to an open question, the question, the rubric and the model answer, for formative homework that does not count toward the report grade.
loop.output: A suggested rubric score and a two-sentence feedback comment quoting the answer.
loop.check: The teacher sees every answer next to the suggestion; a random 10% is marked blind by the teacher first; if agreement falls below the level the department set, suggestions switch off for that assignment.
loop.stop: One suggestion per answer; answers that are unreadable or off-rubric go straight to the teacher.
loop.why_not_simpler: Open answers vary in wording; keyword rules cannot judge whether the reasoning meets the rubric.

steps.what: Teacher writes feedback comments on the work
Teacher enters grades in the student information system
Teacher answers students' questions about their marks

tasks.design: Closed items run as quizzes in the {LMS} and mark themselves; for formative homework, a bounded model step suggests a rubric score and comment per open answer, which the teacher accepts or changes with a blind double-marked sample as a guard. Counting tests stay fully teacher-marked; approved marks sync from the {LMS} to the student information system ({OTHER}).
tasks.previous_blocker: Open answers could not be marked by rules, and paper work had to be marked and typed in by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning environments mark closed items, and pilots show models suggesting scores for open questions that teachers check.
tasks.still_hard: Marks that count are high-risk under the AI Act from December 2027; machine scoring has drawn mass rescoring requests elsewhere, and few teachers use AI for marking yet.
tasks.human_edge: Judging reasoning, spotting a misconception and writing the one comment that helps a student improve.

ambition.what: Feedback on every homework assignment within two days, instead of only on tests.

tasks.altitude: The teacher reviews suggestions and decides every mark; marking time shifts to feedback and follow-up.

reach.learn: Whether blind double-marking keeps agreement high when assistants review suggestions.

evidence.claim: A Dutch test provider's tool suggests scores for open questions in a pilot with seven teachers; one says 1.5 hours of marking took under 15 minutes.
In October 2026, 7% of secondary teachers used AI for marking, against 31% who expected to in 2023.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk, with duties from 2 December 2027; marks that count fall here.
Texas machine-scores state tests; rescoring requests rose from 2,758 in 2024 to 64,489 in 2026, and computers first scored 58% of over 13,300 raised reading scores.

assumptions: Boundary: from assigning work to grades recorded and questions answered; report cards are outside.
Input contract: answer keys and rubrics written by the teacher or department; student work submitted in the {LMS}; fallback is paper marking.
Scenario: about 60% of closed work runs as quizzes; suggestions are used only for formative work.
Student time is outside the teacher's savings.
unknowns: Whether the school allows a model service on student work, and under which DPIA.
research_questions: How often does the teacher change a suggested score, by question type?

already_counted.description: Teacher checks every suggested score against the answer.

incremental.description: Teacher blind-marks the 10% sample and keeps rubrics current.
School IT and the department monitor agreement rates and the model service.

approvals.approved_version: Grade list for the assignment as confirmed by the teacher in s4; a changed mark needs a new confirmation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If most work stays on paper or the school limits suggestions to a few assignments, as low uptake suggests, savings stay near closed-item marking only.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher keeps teaching, mentoring and every marking decision; drafting outlines, slides and comments shifts to review.
reach: Teaching assistants' marking of practice work
skills_to_grow: Reviewing drafted outlines and slides critically
Writing rubrics that a suggestion step can follow
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who gives feedback on every assignment within days, keeps course outlines current each term, and spends mentor time on the students who need it.

job.title: Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education
